newsitem.title: GERMANY: German express, parcels prices mostly stable in '9.
newsitem.headline: German express, parcels prices mostly stable in '9.

text.p: Transport prices for German parcels and express consignments will remain mostly stable in 1997, market players said.
Leading companies offering express and parcels services were mostly keeping prices at last year's levels, the Third European courier, express and parcels congress in Bonn heard.

Moderator Frank Schnell, editor of Deutsche Verkehrs Zeitung, said an industry survey had show both UPS and Deutsche Post AG were not increasing prices while competitor German Parcel was considering a moderate third-quarter price hike.
A spokeswoman for the largest private German parcels service, Deutscher Paket Dienst (DPD), told Reuters that prices would be increased by 3-5 percent this year.
"The increases are being phased in gradually during the year during negotiations with clients," she said.
DHL spokesman Holger Weishaupt added: "We will not change our prices this year."
DHL had control of its costs, investments had been paid off and there was no market need for higher prices, he explained.
Gerhard Pfeffermann, state secretary in the German post and telecommunications, said in a speech that liberalisation of the postal market should lead to lower prices for consumers.
The end of the Deutsche Post monopoly from January 1, 1998, for letters weighing more than 100g or costing more than five marks offered a new market for private companies, he added.
"In the medium-term, we expect lower prices from the opening of the post market and more jobs through more competition," he said.
